opportunity: mTG catalyzes homogeneous, site-specific coupling of cytotoxic payloads to antibodies (via native Q295 or engineered LLQG/Q-tags), giving defined drug-to-antibody ratios and higher therapeutic index than random lysine/cysteine chemistry.
tg_fit: mTG used as the conjugation enzyme (crosslinking/transamidation). Commercially advanced as a bioconjugation platform (Innate Pharma BTG tech, Sanofi collaboration); this is the most mature biotech TG use.
evidence: mTG-based site-specific conjugation yields homogeneous DAR 2:1/4:1 ADCs with preserved cytotoxicity; Innate Pharma licensed its bacterial-TG conjugation platform to Sanofi for next-generation ADCs.

sources.title: Efficient Site-Specific Antibody-Drug Conjugation by Engineering a Nature-Derived Recognition Tag for Microbial Transglutaminase
Innate Pharma and Sanofi collaborate on next generation ADCs using Innate's site-specific conjugation technology
Tag-free, specific conjugation of glycosylated IgG1 antibodies using microbial transglutaminase

verification.note: Multiple peer-reviewed methods plus an active pharma partnership confirm commercial maturity.

opportunity: mTG tags antibodies with an azide linker for click coupling to DBCO-oligonucleotides, producing chemically defined antibody-siRNA/ASO conjugates (ARCs) for targeted nucleic-acid delivery.
tg_fit: mTG as conjugation enzyme (crosslinking). Research/early-preclinical tool; extends the ADC platform to oligonucleotide payloads.
evidence: Two-step mTG azide tagging plus strain-promoted click chemistry gives site-selective, soluble antibody-oligonucleotide conjugates avoiding heterogeneous chemical coupling.

sources.title: Site Selective Antibody-Oligonucleotide Conjugation via Microbial Transglutaminase
Site-directed antibody conjugation methods 1: application of transglutaminase (AbOliGo)

verification.note: Peer-reviewed method plus commercial reagent provider corroborate; still preclinical.

opportunity: mTG site-specifically attaches alkylamino-PEG (or HES) to reactive glutamines on therapeutic proteins, extending plasma half-life and stability without random chemical modification.
tg_fit: mTG as conjugation enzyme (crosslinking). Research stage; an enzymatic alternative to chemical PEGylation.
evidence: Transglutaminase mediates site-specific PEGylation of pharmaceutical proteins at glutamine residues, and thermostable mTG variants conjugate HES to rHuEPO.

sources.title: Site-specific modification and PEGylation of pharmaceutical proteins mediated by transglutaminase
Biotechnological Applications of Transglutaminases

verification.note: Established in literature and reviews; no marketed TG-PEGylated product identified.

opportunity: mTG installs fluorophores, biotin, or bioorthogonal handles onto proteins at single glutamine sites for imaging, pulldown, and functional-tool creation under mild conditions.
tg_fit: mTG as labeling enzyme (crosslinking/transamidation). Research and reagent-scale tool; engineered mTG variants give high site-specificity.
evidence: An engineered mTG enables highly site-specific protein labeling, and simple mTG protocols azide- or biotin-label proteins for downstream capture.

sources.title: Discovery of a microbial transglutaminase enabling highly site-specific labeling of proteins
Site-specific protein labelling and immobilization mediated by microbial transglutaminase (Chem. Commun.)

opportunity: mTG biotinylates or tethers antibodies at the Fc glutamine so they immobilize in a uniform orientation on sensor surfaces, boosting antigen-binding capacity and assay sensitivity.
tg_fit: mTG as coupling enzyme (crosslinking). Research stage; enables oriented capture layers for immunoassays and biosensors.
evidence: Enzyme-mediated site-specific Fc biotinylation gives oriented immobilization on streptavidin surfaces with enhanced antigen-binding versus random coupling.

sources.title: Oriented Surface Immobilization of Antibodies Using Enzyme-Mediated Site-Specific Biotinylation (Langmuir)
Scope of Microbial Transglutaminase for Site-Specific and Oriented Immobilization of Native Antibodies from Various Host Species

opportunity: Transglutaminase forms head-to-tail isopeptide bonds to cyclize peptides, improving proteolytic stability and target affinity for peptide therapeutics and display-library screening.
tg_fit: TG (microbial/tissue) as cyclization enzyme (crosslinking). Research stage; competes with polymerization side reactions.
evidence: Transglutaminase-catalyzed enzymatic cyclization produces macrocyclic peptides, and helicity-dependent TG cyclization has been demonstrated for display-selected ligands.

sources.title: Enzymatic cyclisation of peptides with a transglutaminase
Helicity-Dependent Enzymatic Peptide Cyclization

verification.note: Demonstrated in literature; niche relative to other macrocyclization enzymes.

opportunity: TG crosslinks glutamine-lysine motifs (e.g. QLK/Q-K tags) in engineered protein polymers and self-assembling peptides to form injectable, tunable, in-situ-gelling hydrogels for delivery, biosensing scaffolds, and wound dressings.
tg_fit: mTG or TG2 as crosslinking enzyme. Research/preclinical; recombinant TG substrates allow programmable mechanics.
evidence: Modular TG-crosslinked protein-polymer hydrogels gel in situ, and TG2 self-catalytically crosslinks self-assembled collagen fibril hydrogels for wound-healing applications.

sources.title: Modular enzymatically crosslinked protein polymer hydrogels for in situ gelation
Feasibility of Tissue Transglutaminase for Self-Catalytic Cross-Linking of Self-Assembled Collagen Fibril Hydrogel (ACS Omega)

verification.note: Multiple peer-reviewed studies; overlaps but distinct from tissue-engineering scaffold map.

opportunity: TG2 is the dominant autoantigen in celiac disease; anti-tissue-transglutaminase IgA ELISA is the first-line, high-sensitivity/specificity screening and monitoring test worldwide.
tg_fit: TG2 used as the immobilized capture antigen in the assay (diagnostic reagent, not crosslinking). Fully commercial (marketed IVD kits, e.g. Mayo, multiple ELISA vendors).
evidence: Anti-tTG IgA by ELISA has ~95% sensitivity and >=95% specificity and is the recommended first-line celiac test at any age.

sources.title: IgA antibodies to tissue transglutaminase: An effective diagnostic test for celiac disease
Tissue Transglutaminase Antibody, IgA, Serum - Mayo Clinic Laboratories
Diagnostic Accuracy of IgA Anti-Transglutaminase for Celiac Disease: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis

verification.note: Systematic review plus marketed clinical assays.

opportunity: Prophylactic IV Factor XIII concentrate replaces the missing crosslinking clotting factor, preventing life-threatening (e.g. intracranial) bleeding in congenital FXIII deficiency.
tg_fit: FXIIIa is the plasma transglutaminase; therapy SUPPLIES the crosslinking enzyme (fibrin stabilization) - not inhibition. Fully marketed (Corifact/Fibrogammin P, CSL Behring).
evidence: FDA-approved Corifact (Fibrogammin P) is an effective, well-tolerated prophylaxis dosed ~40 IU/kg every 4 weeks with no spontaneous bleeds over 52 weeks.

sources.title: CSL Behring Receives FDA Approval of Corifact for Congenital Factor XIII Deficiency
Corifact/Fibrogammin P in prophylactic treatment of hereditary factor XIII deficiency (prospective study)

verification.note: FDA approval plus prospective clinical study.

opportunity: Recombinant FXIII A-subunit provides an animal-plasma-free, once-monthly prophylaxis for congenital FXIII A-subunit deficiency.
tg_fit: FXIIIa transglutaminase replacement (supplies crosslinking activity, not inhibition). Marketed (Novo Nordisk, FDA-approved 2013).
evidence: FDA approved Tretten (catridecacog) in Dec 2013 for routine prophylaxis; it prevented bleeding in ~90% of patients with monthly dosing.

sources.title: TRETTEN - FDA Approved Blood Products lead page
FDA Approves TRETTEN for Congenital Factor XIII A-Subunit Deficiency (Novo Nordisk)

verification.note: FDA regulatory page plus manufacturer announcement.

sector: FXIII for acquired deficiency / surgical bleeding & wound healing
opportunity: FXIII concentrate is used peri-operatively and in acquired FXIII deficiency (e.g. cardiac/major surgery, poor wound healing) to stabilize clots and reduce bleeding.
tg_fit: FXIIIa supplies fibrin-crosslinking activity (not inhibition). Clinical/off-label use beyond the congenital indication.
evidence: FXIII concentrate has been used successfully to cover surgical procedures in FXIII-deficient patients, and >20 years of pharmacovigilance support its safety.

sources.title: Use of Factor XIII concentrate in patients with congenital FXIII deficiency undergoing surgical procedures
Safety of Factor XIII Concentrate: Analysis of More than 20 Years of Pharmacovigilance Data

verification.note: Peer-reviewed surgical and safety data; broader acquired-deficiency use is still off-label/investigational.

opportunity: An oral small-molecule TG2 inhibitor blocks gluten-peptide deamidation in the gut, attenuating gluten-induced mucosal damage as the first pharmacologic celiac therapy.
tg_fit: TG2 as a DRUG TARGET - therapy INHIBITS transglutaminase (opposite of using mTG as glue). Clinical (Phase 2/2b; licensed to Takeda from Zedira/Dr Falk).
evidence: In a randomized Phase 2 trial ZED1227 significantly attenuated gluten-induced duodenal mucosal damage at all doses versus placebo; it is the first-in-class TG2 inhibitor in clinical evaluation.

sources.title: A Randomized Trial of a Transglutaminase 2 Inhibitor for Celiac Disease (NEJM)
Features of ZED1227: The First-In-Class Tissue Transglutaminase Inhibitor Undergoing Clinical Evaluation for Celiac Disease
Takeda Enters Collaboration and Licensing Agreement with Zedira and Dr. Falk Pharma

verification.note: NEJM RCT plus pharma licensing; clearest INHIBITION opportunity.

opportunity: Selective small-molecule TG2 inhibitors block ECM crosslinking (collagen/fibronectin) and TGF-beta-driven myofibroblast activation, reversing fibrotic remodeling in lung, heart, and kidney.
tg_fit: TG2 as a DRUG TARGET - therapy INHIBITS transglutaminase crosslinking (inverse of glue use). Preclinical across multiple organ models.
evidence: Selective TG2 inhibitors reverse the IPF myofibroblast phenotype and reduce fibronectin/TGF-beta1 deposition, and inhibitor GK921 attenuates bleomycin lung and post-MI cardiac fibrosis in mice.

sources.title: Transglutaminase 2: a novel therapeutic target for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis using selective small molecule inhibitors
Cardiac fibrosis attenuated by blocking transglutaminase 2 with a selective small-molecule inhibitor (Cell Death & Disease)

verification.note: Multiple peer-reviewed preclinical studies; no approved anti-fibrotic TG2 inhibitor yet.

sector: TG2 INHIBITION in cancer (metastasis & drug resistance)
opportunity: Blocking TG2 reverses EMT, cancer stem-cell traits, chemoresistance, and immune-microenvironment remodeling, re-sensitizing tumors (breast, ovarian, colon) to therapy.
tg_fit: TG2 as a DRUG TARGET - therapeutic strategy is INHIBITION (not crosslinking). Preclinical/research; reversible and irreversible inhibitors under development.
evidence: High tumor TG2 drives metastasis and multidrug resistance; knockdown or catalytic inhibition sensitizes cancer cells to apoptosis, with many small-molecule TG2 inhibitors reported.

sources.title: Transglutaminase 2 in breast cancer metastasis and drug resistance (Frontiers)
Tissue transglutaminase: a new target to reverse cancer drug resistance (Amino Acids)

opportunity: TG2 crosslinks aggregation-prone proteins (huntingtin, tau, amyloid-beta, alpha-synuclein); inhibiting it or blocking TG2-fibronectin interaction is proposed for Huntington's, MS, and CNS injury.
tg_fit: TG2 as a DRUG TARGET - INHIBITION approach (inverse of glue). Research/concept with mixed clinical evidence (cysteamine failed in HD).
evidence: TG2 substrates coincide with disease aggregates, but cysteamine (a non-specific TG inhibitor) failed in a randomized HD trial, so benefit in HD/AD/PD is uncertain; cell-impermeant inhibitors are proposed for MS/CNS injury.

sources.title: Transglutaminase 2 as a therapeutic target for neurological conditions (Expert Opin. Ther. Targets)
Pathogenetic Contributions and Therapeutic Implications of Transglutaminase 2 in Neurodegenerative Diseases

verification.note: Strong biological rationale but mixed/negative clinical data; remains speculative.

opportunity: TG2 crosslinks ECM (collagen, fibronectin, osteopontin) and acts as a GTPase/ATPase to drive osteoblast differentiation and matrix mineralization; abnormal TG2 promotes chondrocyte hypertrophy and cartilage calcification in OA (a potential inhibition target).
tg_fit: TG2 crosslinking is required for physiologic mineralization, but pathologic OA calcification suggests INHIBITION as the therapeutic angle. Research/biology stage.
evidence: TG2-knockout chondrocytes fail to calcify while exogenous TG2 increases hypertrophy and mineralization; abnormal ECM TG2 accumulation promotes cartilage calcification linked to osteoarthritis onset.

sources.title: Transglutaminase 2 in cartilage homoeostasis: novel links with inflammatory osteoarthritis (Amino Acids)
Tissue transglutaminase (TG2) activity regulates osteoblast differentiation and mineralization in SAOS-2

verification.note: Well-supported biology; therapeutic translation (inhibition in OA) still exploratory.

opportunity: Restoring keratinocyte transglutaminase-1 (missing in TGM1-deficient lamellar ichthyosis) via topical/intradermal AAV gene therapy or enzyme-replacement cream to rebuild the skin barrier.
tg_fit: TG1 (keratinocyte TG) - therapy SUPPLIES/restores the crosslinking enzyme for cornified-envelope formation (not inhibition, not glue). Preclinical.
evidence: AAV2-TGM1 delivery increased TGM1 mRNA, protein, and enzyme activity in skin models with a favorable safety profile; topical enzyme-replacement creams are also under development.

sources.title: Evaluation of TGM1 Gene Delivery by AAV into Rat and Pig Skin and Safety of ARCI Gene Therapy (IJMS)
A cellular disease model toward gene therapy of TGM1-dependent lamellar ichthyosis (Mol Ther Methods Clin Dev)

verification.note: Peer-reviewed preclinical gene-therapy data; no approved product.

opportunity: Plant TGs crosslink RuBisCO and cell-wall/membrane proteins and regulate photosynthesis, fertilization, senescence, and stress responses - potential targets for crop stress tolerance and yield engineering.
tg_fit: Plant TG as an endogenous crosslinking enzyme; use is exploratory (physiology/agri-biotech), distinct from mTG food/glue uses. Research/concept.
evidence: Plant TGs localize to chloroplasts, cytoplasm and cell wall, act on RuBisCO, and participate in photosynthesis, fertilization and stress responses, suggesting agri-biotech potential.

sources.title: Plant Transglutaminases: New Insights in Biochemistry, Genetics, and Physiology

verification.note: Physiology well described; concrete biotech application is speculative and single-source.
